question: A school had 140 students. They added 32 students. They multiplied by 7 times. They multiplied by 3 times. They removed 2022 students (projections). They added 23 students. Morning classes, afternoon activities, evening events. David had fewer students. Sarah had more. 500 students elsewhere. How many students?
A student had 206 items. They added 8 items. They tripled them. They multiplied by 8 times. They removed 707 items. Someone had a dozen items. How many items?

A musician had 23 songs. They multiplied by 6 times. They removed 13 songs. They removed 43 songs. They added 12 songs. Morning composing, afternoon arranging, evening mastering. Someone had a dozen songs. How many songs?

A collector had 154 items. They removed 21 items. They multiplied by 7 times. They removed 385 items. They divided by 3. They removed 79 items. David had fewer items. Maria had more. The total progressed. How many items?

A manufacturer had 67 units. They multiplied by 4 times. They multiplied by 5 times. They removed 313 units. They added 38 units. They multiplied by 7 times. Morning production, afternoon adjustments, evening inventory. The time was minutes to hours. How many units?

A business had 177 dollars. They multiplied by 4 times. They divided by 2. They removed 143 dollars. They added 13 dollars. Morning transactions, afternoon deposits, evening balance. David had fewer dollars. Sarah had more. How much money?

A farmer had 59 crops. They added 80 crops. They multiplied by 9 times. They added 66 crops. They added 34 crops. They added 27 crops. They removed 678 crops (harvest). David had fewer crops. Maria had more. The total progressed. How many crops?

A collector had 54 items. They added 13 items. They removed 50 items. They doubled them. They multiplied by 4 times. They added 22 items. David had fewer items. Sarah had more. The time was minutes to hours. How many items?

A musician had 173 songs. They multiplied by 7 times. They added 72 songs. They added 76 songs. They added 5 songs. They multiplied by 8 times. Someone had a dozen songs. The time was minutes to hours. How many songs?

A photographer had 210 photos. They multiplied by 9 times. They added 32 photos. They multiplied by 5 times. They removed 5456 photos (purge). They added 4 photos. 200 photos elsewhere. The time was minutes to hours. How many photos?

A chef had 109 portions. They tripled them. They added 14 portions. They multiplied by 9 times. They removed 1933 portions. David had fewer portions. Maria had more. The total progressed. How many portions?

A factory had 169 units. They tripled them. They multiplied by 8 times. They multiplied by 7 times. They added 38 units. They multiplied by 7 times. David had fewer units. Sarah had more. 300 units elsewhere. How many units?

A student had 119 items. They added 10 items. They added 20 items. They multiplied by 8 times. They tripled them. They added 52 items. They multiplied by 4 times. The total progressed. How many items?

A business had 221 dollars. They added 50 dollars. They removed 75 dollars. They added 42 dollars. They tripled them. They removed 49 dollars. Morning transactions, afternoon deposits, evening review. David had fewer dollars. Sarah had more. How much money?
A farm had 91 crops. They removed 88 crops. They added 44 crops. They removed 9 crops. They added 22 crops. They added 30 crops. Morning tending, afternoon watering, evening counting. How many crops?

A factory had 106 units. They multiplied by 8 times. They multiplied by 4 times. They removed 1281 units. They tripled them. They added 49 units. They removed 198 units. 500 units elsewhere. Morning production, afternoon adjustments, evening inventory. How many units?
A chef had 38 portions. They added 55 portions. They removed 19 portions. They removed 54 portions. They divided by 2. David had fewer portions. Sarah had more. How many portions?

A baker had 22 loaves. They added 71 loaves. They added 68 loaves. They added 6 loaves. They multiplied by 8 times. The time was minutes to hours. Morning baking, afternoon sales, evening restocking. How many loaves?
A collector had 43 items. They added 21 items. They multiplied by 6 times. They added 10 items. They added 4 items. They removed 189 items. The total progressed. 100 items elsewhere. How many items?

Alex is tallying his garden expenses in minutes, which he will later convert to hours. He starts with 233 minutes of work time. He multiplies his effort by 5 days of work, giving him 1165 units. He then loses 1068 minutes due to weather delays. The next day he gains 3 minutes of extra work time. Finally, he adds 11 more minutes. How much total time, in minutes, did Alex accumulate?

Jordan and Casey are running a catering business. Jordan starts with 23 portions of salad. On day 1, the recipe is tripled, making 69 portions. On day 2, the batch is doubled to 138 portions. On day 3, it is multiplied by 7 to reach 966 portions. Finally, 59 more portions are added for a last-minute event. How many portions does Jordan end up with?

Emma has 115 dollars in her bakery fund. She doubles her investment by getting a loan, now having 230 dollars. She then spends 200 dollars on ingredients, leaving 30 dollars. Next, she loses 18 dollars to spoilage. Finally, she adds 23 dollars from a small sale. Her partner has 50 dollars. How much money does Emma have at the end?

A library shelf starts with 36 books. During the morning, 52 more books are added. By afternoon, another 32 books arrive. By evening, 58 more books are shelved. However, 62 books are then returned to the storage room. The neighboring shelf has 100 books. How many books remain on this shelf?

Lisa has 13 candies. She receives 41 more, bringing her to 54 candies. She then shares them equally among 6 friends, leaving each with 9 candies and her with 9 candies (54 divided by 6). She keeps 4 groups worth, giving her 36 candies. Finally, she eats 8 candies. How many candies does Lisa have remaining?

Tom starts his chocolate business with 232 units of inventory. He multiplies by 8 over a week (1856 units). He then divides by half (sharing with a partner), leaving him 928. He loses 467 to spoilage, leaving 461. He gains 19 more units. He multiplies sales by 8 for a wholesale order (3688 units). Finally, he pays out 2900 in costs. How much inventory value remains?
